title: crew rounds refuse a stale head, gates record their own results, a stopped round takes its crew with it, and the reviewer sees the worker's report
acceptance: Four failures from 2026-09-25 each cost rounds, and each was worked around by hand in firstmate's scratchpad. They are listed below, one per item. Its own spec file, design/tasks/T-107.json, is committed on this branch.

1. Stale local head. gh pr update-branch moves only the remote branch, and fm-review.sh, fm-gate.sh and fm-worker.sh read the local branch. So T-068, T-086 and T-104 were approved and gated on heads that were no longer the pull request's. Before a round, each script compares the local branch with origin/<branch>. When the local branch is an ancestor and the task worktree is clean, it fast-forwards. Otherwise it refuses with a message naming both SHAs. Every review verdict and gate summary names the SHA it judged, and that SHA is the pull request's head at the time.

2. Gate summary writer. design.md says nothing writes state/gates/<task>-<sha>.txt. fm-gate.sh writes its own stdout lines there for the head it judged, on every run including a partial --only, and fm-run.sh stops sending that output to /dev/null.

3. A stopped round takes its crew with it. Killing the launcher of a round left its worker or reviewer running: a T-066 worker kept editing to a superseded spec, and a T-104 reviewer posted a verdict on a stale head. bin/fm.sh stop <task> ends that task's live crew runs and their process groups, and records the stop. A reviewer that is stopped, or whose head moved while it ran, posts no verdict.

4. The worker's report reaches the reviewer. Nothing is put into the diff. fm-worker.sh already posts the worker's comment through its say() path. It now marks that comment with a line WORKER-REPORT:<task>. fm-review.sh hands the reviewer every WORKER-REPORT comment posted since the last review verdict, verbatim and fenced with a per-run nonce, as T-073 does for the ask and closed lists. It is labelled as claims by the worker to verify, not evidence by themselves: a run-mode reviewer re-runs a stated search in its checkout. The reviewer skill says so. No other pull request comment is handed over.

Evidence is the required GitHub check and the seven gates, checked by firstmate at the merge gate. Tests written to fail first (a new tests/stop.test.sh for fm.sh stop) cover: a local branch behind origin is fast-forwarded, and a diverged one is refused; the gate summary file is written for the head judged; fm.sh stop leaves no crew process alive; a stale-head reviewer posts nothing; the WORKER-REPORT comments since the last verdict, and only those, reach the prompt fenced. Any gh stub answers exactly as gh does. The worker does not run the suite itself.
